Findings are numbered F51 onward in scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md, continuing the series from the 2026-08-23 stress test. Drive items and fix items alternate deliberately, so that death at any hour costs at most one drive's worth of unfixed findings.

queue.title: Cold start: a fresh project through the whole setup path
queue.detail: Create a NEW project outside the repository and drive the cold-start path that ledger-stress can no longer exercise, because it already has everything. Use the harness: `cd .claude/skills/e2e-loop && AW_HUB_DB="C:/Users/huida/.agentweave/hub/profiles/beta/agentweave.db" py -3.11 e2e.py setup drive-2026-08-26`. Then seed the directory with a REAL subject - a small Python module with three deliberately seeded defects the tests do not cover, the way `ledger` was built - because make-work fixtures never reach the parts of AgentWeave that decide whether work is GOOD. Register two agents on the two cheap runners (Haiku 4.5 and gpt-5.4-mini): `e2e.py agent <proj> author <charter-substring> claude claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` and `e2e.py agent <proj> reviewer <charter-substring> codex gpt-5.4-mini`. TWO runners is not optional - the first run of this skill found a defect that affected only Claude and would have reported the product healthy on one runner. Watch specifically: do the seeded charters attach and do the default runners appear; does the board come up empty and coherent rather than half-populated. Two things are ALREADY MEASURED during prep and do not need re-testing - POST /projects/open adopts main_branch correctly (F4 fires; read it from GET /projects/{id}/settings, NOT from the projects list, which omits the field), and the marker lands at .agentweave/project.json in the new directory carrying {version, project_id} and nowhere else. Record every friction as F51+ in scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md with the request and the row that proves it. If a step has no API, that absence IS the finding - write it down and continue, never paper over it in the harness.
queue.verify: e2e.py state <new-proj> shows the project, both agents bound to their runners, and a clean board; the new project's directory contains .agentweave/project.json and the repository root's git status is still clean.

queue.title: Drive the spec flow: document to materialised tasks
queue.detail: On the Q1 project, drive document creation through to tasks, entirely through the real surface. `e2e.py doc-new`, then trigger the author agent on the document and let it interview you. Play the operator HONESTLY: answer decisively, in prose, with actual constraints - and DELIBERATELY LEAVE ONE ask_user QUESTION UNANSWERED. That is method, not laziness: a tester who answers everything never discovers which questions silently evaporate, and the single most valuable finding in this skill's first run came from a question that was never answered. Then drive the operator gates: close-exploration, propose, approve (`e2e.py close|propose|phase`). Watch the seams, which is where the defects are: between exploring and proposing; between an approved document and a task; whether requirements materialise into tasks with a real dependency graph; whether the unanswered question blocks, times out, or vanishes. Read what the agent ACTUALLY SAID - the transcript is evidence, and on the first run an agent correctly reported it could not do something the tool surface claimed it could. Verify against the database rows, not the chat: document_events, task rows, transitions. Number findings F51+ continuing from Q1.
queue.verify: Tasks exist on the board, traceable to requirements in the approved document; every claim in the log is backed by a row id or a transcript quote.

queue.title: Fix pass 1 - everything severity A from Q1 and Q2
queue.detail: Fix every severity-A finding (wrong behaviour an operator will act on) that Q1 and Q2 produced, each with a regression test, on this branch. Defer B and C to Q6 unless a B is a one-line fix sitting in a file you are already editing. THE RULE THAT GOVERNS THIS ITEM, because it is this repository's dominant failure mode: a fix that passes its tests and cannot fire in production. F41, F43, F45 and F49 were each an instance. So for every fix, MUTATION-CHECK IT - disable the line the test exists for and watch a NAMED test fail - and where the finding was found live, VERIFY IT LIVE against the running Hub, not only against a fixture. A fixture that builds what the product does not build proves nothing; that exact sentence is F43's write-up, and F43's own first implementation then reproduced it and was caught only by querying the live database. Commit each finding's fix separately so the morning diff is readable per finding.

Confirm from the rows: a checkpoint appears carrying a loop_id, its note is the AUTHOR's (F44) and not merely the loop's newest, and the next agent's briefing actually contains it. REMEMBER TO DISABLE THE JOB WHEN THE ITEM ENDS - a loop left enabled spends all night. While here, also watch F12's shape (a loop firing every minute while finished work waits for review) and whether loop-becomes-a-flow's claimable-by-a-different-agent change actually resolved it. Cheap runners ONLY.

queue.title: F50 - render the probe failure (PRE-AUTHORISED by the operator)
queue.detail: The operator authorised this fix during prep, choosing it over parking it. A checkpoint that FAILED its own probe - meaning the model's written summary was checked against the Hub's computed envelope and contradicted it - is briefed to the reviewer as though it passed. render_checkpoint surfaces neither status nor probe_status, and neither checkpoint selector filters on them. Measured rate on the only live sample that exists: 1 of 2. The chosen fix is RENDER THE FAILURE, not skip the checkpoint: the computed half is the Hub's own and stays accurate, so discarding it to avoid a bad paragraph is the more expensive error. Change is in hub/hub/checkpoint_generation.py render_checkpoint (~line 271, where checkpoint.body is appended around line 331) to state status and probe_status, plus a test. Then close task 14.7 in openspec/changes/loop-becomes-a-flow/tasks.md with the evidence, and record the resolution under F50 in scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md. Verify LIVE if Q4 produced a failed checkpoint to render; if it did not, say so rather than claiming live verification.
queue.verify: A named test fails when the status line is removed; npx openspec validate loop-becomes-a-flow --strict stays valid.

queue.title: Drive the operator-in-the-loop surfaces, then vary one axis
queue.detail: Two parts. FIRST, the surfaces where the product deliberately stops and asks: trigger a run with overrides {"permission_mode": "manual"} so Claude routes through --permission-prompt-tool and Codex through decide_approval, and answer the approval card through the real API. Then let a permission card and an ask_user batch TIME OUT rather than answering - AW_DECISION_TIMEOUT and AW_QUESTION_TIMEOUT come from Agent.permission_timeout_seconds and Agent.question_timeout_seconds - and record what the operator sees when they do. Remember there is deliberately NO BACKSTOP behind these and F38's detector was retired on purpose; a turn that ends without calling ask_user has ended, and that is the design, not a bug. Also check F14: a run blocked on an unanswered ask_user should not read in_progress with blocked_reason null. SECOND, Step 6 of the e2e-loop method - vary ONE environmental axis and re-run a verification. PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 is the one with a track record: the first run's tests passed 99/99 and failed 9 under it, and a two-agent review was structurally incapable of noticing because both agents shared one machine. Locale, working directory or a different runner are the alternatives.
queue.verify: The approval card answered through the API and the run continuing; the timeout path observed with its actual elapsed time; the varied axis re-run reported with its real output, pass or fail.

queue.detail: Full verification and the write-up. Run: py -3.11 -m pytest hub/tests/ -q (background it, about 22 minutes); py -3.11 -m pytest tests/ -q; py -3.11 -m ruff check src/ hub/ tests/; black --check src/ hub/hub/ hub/tests/ tests/ --target-version py311; npx openspec validate --changes --strict. Read the full diff for accidental legacy revival, generated debris and unrelated files. Write openspec/explorations/2026-08-26-driving-everything.md ranked by what each finding COST, each with its evidence, each labelled one-defect-or-design-gap, and record WHAT HELD as well - a gate that correctly refused something is a result the next session needs. Then the morning summary in the log: what landed per finding id, what did not and why, what to distrust, and what surprised you.

dead_ends: The bash heredoc mangles \n inside Python string literals - writing an escaped newline through `python - <<'PYEOF'` produces a REAL newline and a SyntaxError. Use the Write/Edit tools for any content with escapes or backticks.
`gh run list --limit 1` returns whichever workflow finished first, not CI. Select by name: gh run list --json name,status,conclusion,databaseId.

GET /projects/{id} does not return checkpoint_runner_id - it is a settings field, and reading it there returns None for a project that has one set. PATCH /projects/{id} is 405; the route is PUT /projects/{id}/settings.
AIJob has no `schedule` field (it is `cron` plus `session_mode`); Loop has no `label` (it is `purpose`); Checkpoint.body is Text, a markdown string, not the notes dict.
A test asserting 'notes consumed' scoped to the completing conversation is vacuous once the fixture puts the note elsewhere - it finds nothing and passes while proving nothing. Assert by note id.

A flow job is session_mode: new, so EVERY firing gets its own conversation. A task needing more than one firing records its notes in one conversation and its completion in another, routinely. Any gate that requires them to be in the same conversation cannot fire in production.
run.task_id is NULL on most runs carrying a completed transition - read the transition table instead, never run.task_id.

The full hub suite takes about 11 minutes, MEASURED 2026-08-26 (672s for 3127 tests) - older handoffs say 22-23 and that figure is stale. Either way, background it and keep working; do not conclude it is stuck.

NEW, measured and FIXED during this prep: e2e.py's `clean` used shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True), which on Windows is a lie - git marks everything under .git/objects read-only, rmtree raises on the first one, the error is swallowed, and `clean` prints 'removed' over a directory that is still there. Now goes through _rmtree_windows, which clears the read-only bit and REPORTS if the tree survives anyway. Verified causally on the leftover directory the old code had abandoned.

main_branch is not on GET /api/v1/projects or GET /projects/{id} - it is on GET /projects/{id}/settings, like checkpoint_runner_id. Reading it from the list returns None for a project that has it set, which looks exactly like F4 having failed.
ruff is not on PATH in Git Bash - use py -3.11 -m ruff. black IS on PATH but needs --target-version py311 (this machine's black runs under 3.11 and the codebase targets 3.12).
pytest --timeout= is unavailable - no pytest-timeout plugin. sqlite3 is not on PATH - use py -3.11 -c with file:<path>?mode=ro. A sleep longer than a few minutes is blocked in the Bash tool.

The aw.py driver in scripts/drive is imported by path - every py -3.11 -c "from aw import ..." must run from scripts/drive/. Its API is api(method, path, body=None) returning (status, parsed); aw.P is empty unless AW_PROJECT is set.

agentweave cannot be started from the repository ROOT at all: -m puts the cwd on sys.path[0] and this repo's own hub/ directory shadows the installed hub package. Start from hub/.

npx openspec validate needs --all --strict or a named change. openspec requires SHALL/MUST on a requirement's OPENING line, not merely somewhere in its body - the validator reads only the first physical line.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (Q4 close, iteration 7): a Loop's `stop_when_queue_empties` is evaluated on the NEXT scheduler tick, not synchronously the instant the last task in its queue reaches a terminal status - a job whose cron will never fire again (this iteration deliberately used one) can sit with an empty, fully-completed queue and `enabled: true` indefinitely, with nothing self-correcting it. Very likely harmless for a real cron (it would tick and self-stop normally) but means a loop must never be assumed to have disabled itself just because its queue looks empty - always disable explicitly, per the standing rule, rather than trusting the stop condition to have already fired.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (F55): on this machine, datetime.now(timezone.utc) returns the IDENTICAL value across five consecutive calls with no delay - Windows clock resolution is coarser than the microsecond precision the value implies. Any ORDER BY created_at DESC with a non-monotonic secondary sort (id.desc(), where id is a random short_id()) can silently pick the wrong 'latest' row on a timestamp tie. latest_checkpoint_for_loop (hub/hub/checkpoints.py) has exactly this shape and is now F55, unfixed - test_flow_checkpoint_lineage.py flakes on it (confirmed pre-existing, not caused by any change this session): 2 of 6 bare re-runs failed on the unmodified branch tip. If this file is ever red, re-run it once before treating it as a new regression, and do not 'fix' it by loosening the assertion - the ordering bug is real.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (F56, iteration 8): InboundQueueEntry.state only becomes 'delivered' atomically WITH a Run's creation (inbound_queue.py's deliver helper). A TriggerAgentError raised inside trigger_agent_directly BEFORE that point (an unresolvable review_task_id, an archived agent, any other pre-flight refusal) leaves the entry state='queued' forever with delivery_attempts stuck at 0, because return_run_entries (the thing that counts attempts and abandons at DELIVERY_ATTEMPT_LIMIT) only runs for a Run that was created and then failed post-spawn. schedule_agent always retries the SAME oldest queued entry first regardless of what a new trigger asked for, so one such poisoned entry wedges an agent's entire queue indefinitely with a misleading 'queued' response naming an unrelated task. Fixed in hub/hub/turn_scheduler.py this iteration - if a future session sees an agent stuck on a nonsensical waiting_reason, check inbound_queue_entries for an old queued entry sitting ahead of everything else before assuming anything else is wrong.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (iteration 10): scripts/drive/aw.py's api() ALREADY prepends /api/v1 - passing a path that also starts with /api/v1 double-prefixes and 404s silently (looks like 'project not found' or 'not found', not an obviously-wrong-URL error). Pass paths like /projects/{id}/tasks, not /api/v1/projects/{id}/tasks. Also: the evidence routes are doubly-nested by the router composition - full path is /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/project/spec/evidence (not /projects/{id}/evidence, not /projects/{id}/spec/evidence) - spec.py's router has prefix="/project" (singular) and is itself mounted under project_resources_router's /projects/{project_id}. e2e.py's project argument to `turn`/`task-set`/etc. must be the project ID (proj-xxxx), not the human slug used by `state` in some contexts - ledger-stress as a literal string 404s on POST endpoints.

NEW, measured 2026-08-26 (iteration 8): after unblocking a wedged agent, expect a self-drain - the completion path reschedules the same agent, so backlogged entries can fire several more real runs with no further triggering. Check `runs`/`task_transitions` afterward rather than assuming only the run you explicitly watched happened; this iteration found a third task moved to revision_needed this way that nobody had gone looking for.
method_reminders: Use the real surface. Never simulate a step. If something has no API, that absence IS the finding - write it down and continue. This is how 'no integration step exists' surfaced.
Play the operator honestly, and leave something unanswered. A tester who answers everything never discovers which questions silently evaporate.

Watch the seams: between exploring and proposing, between an approved document and a task, between a completed task and a reviewed one, between one agent and the next. The defects are there, not inside a phase.
Read what the agent actually said. The transcript is evidence. Do not dismiss an agent's account of its own failure - verify it.
Follow peer-triggered work, not just what you triggered. Runs an agent starts by messaging another take a different path through the code, and that is where posture and continuity get lost.

Never accept 'the tests pass' as evidence. Run them yourself, then recompute a result by hand and compare. Check the rows, not the chat: an agent's summary of what it did is a claim, the rows are the fact.
A green suite agrees with broken behaviour more often than you expect. Mutation-check anything you claim: delete the line the test exists for, and watch a NAMED test fail.
The best evidence is the failure you did not stage. Watch for unprovoked failures and write them up when they happen.
Say when you contaminated your own test. Testing code you wrote yourself inherits your blind spots - a finding you did NOT make is weaker evidence, and the operator needs to know which is which.
Record what HELD, not only what broke. A gate that correctly refused something is a result the next session needs.
